current.text: He is projected to start at guard next to Tyrese Haliburton, with Nesmith, Siakam and Zubac.
With Haliburton back, he moves into a lower-usage role and his assists should drop.
His only real upside comes if Haliburton misses time.
Experts see him as a safe veteran with little or no upside. They would rather take upside fliers at the same spot.
Experts call him a fade at his Yahoo rank of about 108. They see his ESPN rank of about 149 as reasonable.
Experts think pick 120 is too early. They put his fair spot in rounds 13 to 14, around pick 164. One expert would not draft him in standard leagues but sees him as fine in deeper leagues.
His Yahoo injury status is questionable, with an undisclosed reason.
Indiana plays 3, 4 and 3 games in our fantasy playoff weeks, which is not ideal. The team has 15 back-to-backs.
Coach Rick Carlisle keeps minutes low even for healthy players and rests players on back-to-backs.
Experts project Indiana to win 46 to 48 games and finish as a top-six seed in the East.

durable.text: Assists are his one strong category. His assist value depends on Haliburton being out.
He is a low-usage player with up and down shooting percentages and weak defensive stats.
He is a poor three-point shooter in the regular season but has shot about 40% from three in the playoffs.

note: With Haliburton back, he is an assists-only guard (6.1 projected assists, z +1.5) with no other real strength, and his playoff schedule is weak. His prices are near the minimum (Yahoo value 3 USD at an average cost of 1.0 USD, ESPN 0 USD), and experts put his fair spot around pick 164, so do not repeat last season's 10 USD price. At most, take him for 1 USD late. Better, leave him on waivers, check his Q status, and add him fast if Haliburton's minutes are limited or he misses time.
